passage.bullet: Sumer, the Indus Valley, Shang China, and Egypt all grew beside life-giving rivers
Yearly summer inundation floods soaked dry banks → stopped desert sand burying Egypt
Sinking floodwaters left fertile Kemet black silt → created farmland beside barren Deshret desert

context.bullet: Almost no rain fell in Egypt → villagers relied completely on southern African rains
Rich river mud fed growing villages → allowed early towns, trade, and kingship

stems.stem: Around 3500 BC, Ancient Egypt grew beside the ____________ just like early civilisations in ____________, the Indus Valley, and China.
Every summer, the ____________ flood covered the riverbanks and left behind rich black mud called ____________.
Without this fertile Black Land, the scorching ____________ desert would have made growing crops impossible.

lesson_1.watch_out: Kemet meant fertile Black Land from dark river mud, whereas Deshret meant the scorching Red Land desert.

passage.bullet: Wooden shaduf levers with mud counterweights lifted Nile water → watered higher garden plots
Fertile Kemet fields grew wheat and barley → marshes gave flax and papyrus reeds
Wooden boats drifted north on the current and sailed south → linked trading towns

context.bullet: Summer inundation floods refilled ditches and marshes → kept village harvests reliable each year
Flax became cool white linen clothing → papyrus reeds made sandals and writing scrolls

stems.stem: Farmers dug ditches and swung a wooden ____________ lever so they could lift cool water onto ____________.
Damp fields produced ____________ for bread and barley for soup, while marshes supplied ____________ and papyrus.
Traders floated north with the ____________ and raised square sails to travel ____________ between Nile towns.

lesson_1.watch_out: The Nile flows northwards to the sea, so boats drifted north on the current and sailed south with the wind.

passage.bullet: Hilly southern Upper Egypt and marshy northern Lower Egypt → ruled separately for centuries
Southern warrior King Narmer conquered Lower Egypt around 3100 BC → recorded on the Narmer Palette
Rulers combined the white and red crowns into one Double Crown → united one kingdom

context.bullet: One ruler controlling the whole Nile Valley → coordinated grain trade and flood farming
The Nile flows downhill from southern hills to the northern sea → shaped both lands

stems.stem: Because the Nile flows downhill towards the north, hilly southern Egypt was called ____________ while the northern delta was ____________.
Around 3100 BC, southern ruler ____________ marched northwards and carved his triumph onto the ____________.
Joining the white and red crowns into the ____________ showed that Egypt was now one ____________.

lesson_1.watch_out: Upper Egypt is in the south and Lower Egypt is in the north because the River Nile flows downhill northwards.

passage.bullet: Old Kingdom Egyptians honoured pharaohs as living gods → demanded grander eternal tombs
Architect Imhotep stacked six stone layers at Saqqara → created Djoser's Step Pyramid around 2670 BC
Khufu's Great Pyramid used 2.3 million limestone blocks → stood 146 metres tall at Giza

context.bullet: United Nile grain taxes after King Narmer → gave Old Kingdom pharaohs huge building resources
Early kings lay beneath low mud-brick tombs → stacked stone pyramids lasted far longer

stems.stem: Replacing low mud-brick tombs around 2670 BC, royal builder ____________ stacked six stone layers for Pharaoh Djoser at ____________.
Later at Giza, Pharaoh ____________ raised the Great Pyramid to ____________ metres using 2.3 million blocks.
Egyptians built such vast monuments because they believed their pharaoh was a ____________ who brought good floods.

lesson_2.watch_out: Pyramids were giant royal tombs built for the afterlife rather than palaces where living families stayed.

passage.bullet: Masons tapped copper chisels and soaked expanding wooden wedges → split heavy limestone cleanly
Wooden barges floated smooth white Tura limestone across the flooded Nile → reached Giza harbour
Crews poured water ahead of wooden sledges → halved sand friction up sloping ramps

context.bullet: Egyptians had no iron tools, cranes, or wheeled trucks → relied on clever physics
Summer Nile inundation raised water levels → carried heavy stone barges closer to Giza

stems.stem: Inside rocky quarries, masons split heavy limestone using ____________ chisels, wooden mallets, and soaked ____________.
Fine white casing stone from ____________ travelled across the flooded Nile aboard sturdy ____________.
Pouring ____________ onto the desert sand helped hauling crews drag wooden ____________ smoothly up ramps.

lesson_2.watch_out: Pyramid builders had no iron tools or wheeled trucks—they used copper chisels, wooden sledges, and wet sand.

passage.bullet: Giza builders' villages held giant bakeries, cattle bones, and fish → fed valued workers well
Skeletons showed broken bones carefully set and healed → proved workers received skilled medical care
Paid farmers and craftworkers laboured in proud teams → Khafre also carved the Great Sphinx

context.bullet: When summer floods covered Nile fields → peasant farmers earned rations building royal tombs
Khafre's limestone Great Sphinx combined a lion's body and royal head → guarded Giza's tombs

stems.stem: Archaeologists disproved the slave myth by uncovering walled ____________ packed with bakeries, cattle bones, and ____________.
Human skeletons found near Giza had healed ____________, proving that injured builders were treated by ____________.
Skilled craftworkers and ____________ worked in rival crews while Pharaoh ____________ carved the Great Sphinx nearby.

lesson_2.watch_out: Paid farmers and skilled craftworkers built the Giza pyramids—evidence of beef rations and medical care disproved the slave myth.

passage.bullet: God-king Pharaoh ruled at the top → backed by viziers, nobles, and temple priests
Educated scribes counted grain taxes above skilled craftworkers → workshops shaped treasures like blue-glazed William
Millions of peasant farmers stood at the bottom → grew the grain feeding all Egypt

context.bullet: Fertile Kemet flood mud made huge harvests possible → funded royal palaces and temples
Farmers and craftworkers from the lower tiers → supplied the skilled building teams at Giza

stems.stem: At the peak of the social pyramid ruled the ____________, assisted by chief ministers called ____________, nobles, and priests.
Respected ____________ recorded grain taxes, ranking just above skilled ____________ such as potters and jewellers.
Forming the widest base of society, millions of ____________ paid yearly grain taxes that fed everyone.

lesson_3.watch_out: Peasant farmers formed the largest group at the bottom of the social pyramid, yet their grain kept all Egypt alive.

passage.bullet: Whitewashed mud-brick walls and tiny high windows bounced heat away → flat roofs cooled sleepers
Families wore airy white flax linen and papyrus sandals → stayed comfortable in desert heat
Villagers ate flatbread, lentils, onions, and figs → played thirty-square Senet games each evening

context.bullet: Few trees grew beside the desert → ordinary homes used Nile mud while stone built tombs
Nile fields and marshes supplied wheat, flax, and papyrus → shaped daily food and dress

stems.stem: Villagers painted their ____________ houses white to reflect sunlight and slept up on ____________ during hot nights.
Woven flax became light ____________ clothes, while marsh papyrus reeds were braided into ____________.
After eating warm flatbread with figs and lentils, families tossed sticks to race across ____________ boards.

lesson_3.watch_out: Ordinary Egyptians lived in whitewashed mud-brick houses rather than inside stone pyramids or limestone temples.

passage.bullet: Scribes learned over 700 hieroglyphs → knowledge vanished completely centuries after ancient Egypt ended
French soldiers found the 196 BC Rosetta Stone in 1799 → matched hieroglyphs with Ancient Greek
Jean-François Champollion compared Greek ruler names with oval cartouches → unlocked hieroglyphs in 1822

context.bullet: Papyrus scrolls took skill to make → student scribes practised first on broken pottery pieces
Greek-speaking rulers governed Egypt in 196 BC → carved decrees in both Greek and Egyptian

stems.stem: Student scribes practised more than 700 ____________, a sacred script that nobody could read before ____________.
Unearthed by French soldiers in 1799, the ____________ repeated the same royal message in three scripts including ____________.
Scholar ____________ matched Greek royal names to oval ____________ rings to decipher hieroglyphs in 1822.

lesson_3.watch_out: The Rosetta Stone was carved in 196 BC, dug up in 1799, and finally deciphered by Champollion in 1822—do not mix up those three dates.

passage.bullet: Polytheistic Egyptians worshipped Ra, Osiris, Isis, and Horus → jackal-headed Anubis guarded sandy tombs
Every person possessed two spirits called the ka and the winged ba → survived after death
Both spirits needed a recognisable physical home → decayed bodies meant losing eternal afterlife

context.bullet: Horus protected living pharaohs while Osiris ruled the dead → linked royal rule with eternity
Protecting preserved bodies for the ka and ba → drove pharaohs to build lasting tombs

stems.stem: Polytheistic Egyptians worshipped many deities, including underworld ruler ____________ and jackal-headed tomb guardian ____________.
Religious teachings stated that each person's soul had twin spirits known as the ____________ and winged ____________.
If a dead body rotted away inside the tomb, its spirits could not ____________ forever.

lesson_4.watch_out: Polytheistic means worshipping many different gods and goddesses, unlike monotheism which worships only one god.

passage.bullet: Four Canopic jars stored internal organs → priests kept the heart inside for judgement
Dry natron salt absorbed moisture for forty days → stopped the body rotting before wrapping
Priests wrapped oiled linen bandages with a heart scarab → added shabti figures to farm

context.bullet: Flax linen grown beside the Nile → supplied the long bandages needed for seventy-day embalming
Egyptians pictured paradise like fertile Nile fields → packed shabti servants to do farm work

stems.stem: During the seventy-day ritual, priests packed four organs into ____________ and dried the body using ____________ salt.
Embalmers deliberately left the ____________ inside the chest because Egyptians believed it held a person's ____________.
Alongside a protective ____________ charm under the linen wraps, tombs held blue ____________ figures to farm.

lesson_4.watch_out: Priests never placed the heart into a Canopic jar—it stayed inside the chest so it could be weighed in the afterlife.

passage.bullet: Book of the Dead spells guided spirits → Anubis weighed hearts against Ma'at's truth feather
Thoth recorded the verdict → monster Ammit devoured hearts weighed down by cruel deeds
Hearts lighter than the feather passed Osiris → entered the sunny Field of Reeds forever

context.bullet: Scribes painted Book of the Dead spells onto papyrus scrolls → tucked inside wealthy coffins
Fearing Ammit beside the golden scales → encouraged living Egyptians to act kindly and honestly

stems.stem: Guided by ____________ scrolls, the spirit watched Anubis balance its heart against the feather of ____________.
While ibis-headed ____________ wrote down the result, any heavy heart was eaten by the monster ____________.
Kind people with light hearts were welcomed by ____________ into the peaceful ____________.

lesson_4.watch_out: The Book of the Dead was not one single bound book—it was a custom papyrus scroll of spells placed inside a coffin.

passage.bullet: Hatshepsut crowned herself full pharaoh around 1479 BC → wore the striped headcloth and false beard
Five trading ships sailed to Punt → returned with gold, ebony, and living frankincense trees
Grand reliefs at Deir el-Bahari celebrated her Punt voyage → showcased peaceful New Kingdom wealth

context.bullet: Egyptians usually expected male kings → royal beard statues proved Hatshepsut held full divine authority
Living frankincense trees planted at Thebes → supplied sweet-smelling resin for Karnak temple gods

stems.stem: Crowning herself full pharaoh around 1479 BC, ____________ had statues carved wearing the striped headcloth and ____________.
Preferring peaceful trade to war, she sent five ships to the ____________ for gold, ebony, and ____________ trees.
Carvings along her cliff temple at ____________ proudly recorded every treasure her sailors brought home.

lesson_5.watch_out: Hatshepsut ruled as a full crowned pharaoh in her own right rather than merely serving as a king's wife.

passage.bullet: Akhenaten and Nefertiti rejected traditional gods → worshipped only the golden sun-disc called Aten
Royal court abandoned Thebes and Karnak's priests → built a brand-new Nile city at Amarna
Nefertiti led sun offerings and wore a tall blue crown → priests restored old gods afterwards

context.bullet: Egyptians had worshipped Osiris, Isis, and Ra for centuries → sudden religious change angered priests
Sculptor Thutmose carved Nefertiti's painted limestone bust → preserved Amarna's distinctive artistic style

stems.stem: Shocking Egypt's temple priests, Pharaoh ____________ and Queen Nefertiti turned away from old gods to worship ____________.
Leaving Thebes behind, the royal couple constructed a brand-new capital city beside the Nile at ____________.
Although sculptor Thutmose immortalised ____________ in limestone, priests quickly restored traditional worship at ____________ after Akhenaten died.

lesson_5.watch_out: Akhenaten's worship of the sun-disc Aten did not last permanently—priests restored Egypt's traditional gods soon after his death.

passage.bullet: Clashed with Hittite chariots at Kadesh → sealed the world's oldest written peace treaty
Ruled Egypt for sixty-six years → brought long stability after years of border warfare
Carved four twenty-metre statues at Abu Simbel → aligned inner chambers with twice-yearly sunbeams

context.bullet: Royal scribes recorded the 1259 BC Hittite treaty → copies survived on silver and clay
Towering Abu Simbel cliffs stood in southern Egypt → impressed travellers entering along the Nile

stems.stem: Following a fierce chariot clash against the ____________ at Kadesh, Ramesses II signed the world's oldest surviving ____________.
Governing Egypt for ____________ years allowed him to fund grand monuments across the entire Nile Valley.
Builders carved four twenty-metre seated statues into the cliffs at ____________, lit inside twice a year by ____________.

lesson_5.watch_out: Ramesses II did not crush the Hittites outright at Kadesh—neither army won clearly, leading to their 1259 BC peace treaty.

passage.bullet: Rulers abandoned visible pyramids → cut hidden rock tombs inside the Valley of the Kings
Tutankhamun died aged nineteen in 1323 BC → buried inside a modest underground tomb, KV62
Later tomb builders dumped limestone chips over KV62's steps → hid his treasures from thieves

context.bullet: Crowned aged nine after Amarna's upheaval → Tutankhamun restored Egypt's traditional temple gods
Towering Old Kingdom pyramids advertised royal gold → ancient robbers emptied almost every giant tomb

stems.stem: Because giant pyramids attracted thieves, New Kingdom kings carved hidden cliff tombs inside the ____________.
Crowned aged nine around 1332 BC, ____________ restored traditional gods before dying aged nineteen in ____________.
Limestone rubble dumped by later builders buried the steps to ____________, protecting its gold for three thousand years.

lesson_6.watch_out: Tutankhamun was buried in a small underground cliff tomb in the Valley of the Kings rather than inside a pyramid.

passage.bullet: Water-boy Hussein Abdel Rassoul found the top step → Howard Carter and Egyptian excavators cleared KV62
Intact tomb held over 5,000 objects → included gilded chariots, thrones, and Senet boards
Stone sarcophagus protected an eleven-kilogram gold death mask → required ten years of careful cataloguing

context.bullet: Chariots, thrones, and Senet games packed inside KV62 → equipped Tutankhamun's spirit for eternity
Nearly all other royal tombs had been stripped → KV62 revealed complete New Kingdom craftsmanship

stems.stem: In November 1922, water-boy ____________ spotted a buried stone step for ____________ and his Egyptian excavation team.
Peering inside by candlelight, the team found over ____________ intact artefacts including gilded chariots and ____________ boards.
Protected inside a stone ____________ shone an eleven-kilogram gold ____________, and cataloguing everything took ten years.

lesson_6.watch_out: Howard Carter did not dig alone—skilled Egyptian excavators and water-boy Hussein Abdel Rassoul were vital to finding KV62.

passage.bullet: Alexander the Great founded Alexandria in 332 BC → general Ptolemy started Greek-speaking Ptolemaic rule
Cleopatra VII ruled wisely from 51 BC → spoke Egyptian alongside eight other languages
Roman forces defeated Cleopatra's fleet in 30 BC → ended pharaoh rule and made Egypt Roman

context.bullet: Pharaohs had ruled since King Narmer around 3100 BC → lasted three millennia before Rome
Mediterranean Alexandria boasted a giant lighthouse and famous library → blended Greek and Egyptian culture

stems.stem: After ____________ founded coastal Alexandria in 332 BC, his general began the Greek-speaking ____________ dynasty.
Taking the throne in 51 BC, Queen ____________ governed shrewdly and learned ____________ plus eight other languages.
When mighty ____________ defeated Cleopatra's fleet in ____________, three thousand years of rule by pharaohs ended.

lesson_6.watch_out: Cleopatra VII lived closer in time to us today than to Khufu's Great Pyramid—and came from the Greek Ptolemaic dynasty.
